## 论文标题方向
Depth Fingerprinting of Recursive LLM Generation Chains

## One-Sentence Contribution
We formulate ordinal depth estimation for recursive LLM generation chains, showing that distributional features exhibit differential depth response (central-tendency drifts, shape remains stationary), yielding a 7-feature ensemble that reliably classifies generation depth (LOGO F1=0.79) across 6 generators / 3 model families (including 7B+ scale).

## Story Arc
Problem: Web data increasingly contains recursive LLM-generated text of unknown provenance depth. Binary detectors cannot distinguish gen-1 from gen-2+. We characterize differential depth response: level/diversity features drift monotonically with depth, shape features remain near-stationary. 7-feature ensemble LOGO F1=0.79 across 6 generators, significantly outperforming all single-detector baselines (p<0.001). Honest negative: downstream curation does not benefit.

## Framing Rules (MUST FOLLOW)
- Use "differential depth response", NOT "dual dynamics" or "H1/H2"
- Contribution is empirical/conceptual, NOT methodological
- Do NOT call drift/stationarity split a "discovery" — it follows from location-shift properties
- Report realistic performance range (0.69-0.85 per-gen, 0.79 LOGO avg), not just best-case
- Use individual-level Spearman ρ with bootstrap CI, NOT R² on aggregated means
- "Distributional depth profiling" preferred over "distributional fingerprinting"
- Binoculars number = 0.579 (bugfix version from plan-015-v2, not the old value)

### §5.1 Depth Classification Performance (Claim 1)
- 6-gen LOGO F1 = 0.7897 (NOT 0.80), 5-gen baseline = 0.8037
- Per-generator held-out F1 range: 0.69-0.85
  - Pythia-1B: 0.851
  - OLMo-2-1B: 0.752
  - Qwen3-8B: 0.689 (cross-scale transfer gap)
- Family-out Δ = +0.0107 (Pythia vs non-Pythia)
- Gen-0 near-perfect (F1≈0.95), gen-1 vs gen-2+ is the hard distinction
- Bootstrap CI [0.786, 0.799] for ensemble, p<0.001 vs all baselines
- Length not a confound: |ρ|<0.14, normalized trends preserved (plan-013)
- 6-gen LOGO 0.7897 includes Qwen3-8B (8.2B params) — depth signal persists at scale
- Qwen3-8B held-out F1 = 0.6849, CI [0.672, 0.698] — cross-scale gap is real
- Adding 8B data IMPROVES original 5-gen classification (+0.9pp to 0.8086)
Evidence: plan-002-eval, plan-015-v2, plan-014, plan-013. Table 1, Fig 2.

### §5.2 Differential Depth Response (Claim 2)
- entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio: drift monotonically with depth
- entropy_std, tail_decay: near-stationary
- Feature complementarity: full(0.80) > surface(0.75) = reference(0.75), McNemar p≈0
- Also confirmed at 6-gen level: full(0.789) > surface(0.729) > reference(0.745)
- Permutation importance: hapax_ratio(0.271) > ttr(0.165) > entropy_mean(0.156)
- 3 cross-family reference models (Pythia-410M, OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B): LOGO F1 0.80-0.82, drift direction consistent
- DO NOT call this a "discovery" — acknowledge it follows from location-shift properties

- 7-feature ensemble: 0.798, CI [0.786, 0.799]
- Avg-LogProb: 0.765, CI [0.616, 0.820] → +3.9pp, paired bootstrap p=0.000, diff [3.4, 4.4]

- Single CI (e.g. Avg-LogProb [0.59, 0.82]) is wider than all pairwise detector differences — no single detector is reliably best across generators.
Evidence: plan-015-v2. Fig 3.

### §5.4 Downstream Utility — Negative Finding (Claim 3)
- HONEST negative, do NOT hide or spin
- 5 curation variants × 3 seeds, OLMo-2-0425-1B fine-tuning:
  - all (12,299 samples): ppl = 2.335 ± 0.000

- Cross-seed variance <0.002, highly consistent result

This differential response is consistent with recursive generation inducing a **location shift** in the NLL distribution — the text becomes progressively more predictable (mean shifts) while the functional form of the distribution is preserved (shape is invariant). The genuine novelty is not the drift/stationarity split per se (which follows from location-shift properties), but: (a) the **task formulation** (ordinal depth estimation beyond binary detection), (b) **empirical validation** across 6 generators / 3 model families (including 7B+ scale) showing this pattern is robust, (c) the practical consequence that combining both feature types yields **complementary signal** for depth classification (macro-F1 0.79 cross-generator with 6 generators, 0.77 cross-family). Depth signal is scale-invariant as a phenomenon, though cross-scale classifier transfer shows a moderate gap (8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85).\\n\\n## Core Claims (3 条，均可证伪)\\n\\n**Claim 1 — Depth Discriminability**: Distributional features computed under a held-out reference model can classify text generation depth (gen-0 / gen-1 / gen-2+) with macro-F1 significantly above chance, generalizing across unseen generators (leave-one-generator-out evaluation).\\n\\n**Claim 2 — Differential Depth Response & Feature Complementarity**: Depth-dependent features exhibit differential response: central-tendency/diversity features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) drift monotonically with depth (consistent with location shift in NLL distribution), while shape features (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. Full feature set (cross-gen 0.80) significantly outperforms surface-only (0.75) and reference-only (0.75) — the two feature groups are complementary. Notably, reference features generalize better across generators while surface features are stronger in-distribution — demonstrating complementarity across different evaluation axes.\\n\\n**Claim 3 — Downstream Utility (Negative Finding)**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality compared to random subsampling. At equal data count, size_matched (random control, ppl=2.367) outperforms depth01 (depth-stratified, 2.387) and binary_filtered (2.389). The primary determinant is data quantity, not depth composition (all 12K samples → ppl=2.335). Depth fingerprinting is an effective **diagnostic** tool for characterizing provenance, but not a **curative** tool for data curation. This honest negative finding is reported transparently.\\n\\n## Story Spine\\n\\n**Problem**: Web-scraped training data increasingly contains LLM-generated text of unknown provenance depth. Current detection methods offer only binary real-vs-synthetic classification, forcing all-or-nothing filtering: discard everything flagged as synthetic (losing useful gen-1 content) or keep everything (admitting high-risk deep-generation text with compounding distributional drift).\\n\\n**Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (FastDetectGPT, SynthID-Text, LD-Score) cannot distinguish gen-1 from gen-2+. Attractor cycle theory (ACL 2025) proves paraphrasing chains converge to 2-period cycles, bounding depth signal to ~3 classes — but this result depends on the semantic-preservation constraint of paraphrasing. No existing work attempts generation depth estimation. When repurposed as ordinal depth predictors, single detector scores (Avg-LogProb 0.77, LD-Score 0.72) show moderate signal but **high cross-generator variance** (CIs spanning 0.59–0.82), making them unreliable as standalone depth estimators.\\n\\n**Our framing**: We characterize distributional drift in recursive non-paraphrastic LLM generation, revealing **differential depth response**: level/diversity features (including reference-model entropy_mean) drift monotonically with depth, while distributional shape features (entropy variance, tail decay) remain near-stationary. This split is about **what the feature measures** (central tendency vs shape), not where it comes from. The combination of drifting and stationary features yields a 7-feature ensemble (LOGO F1=0.80 [0.786, 0.799]) that **significantly and consistently** outperforms all single-detector baselines (p<0.001 vs Avg-LogProb 0.77, LD-Score 0.72, FastDetectGPT 0.63, Binoculars 0.58). Crucially, single detectors exhibit high cross-generator variance (CIs spanning 0.59–0.82), while our ensemble maintains tight consistency — the practical advantage is **reliability across unknown generators**, not just average performance.\\n\\n**Headline result template**: \\\"On multi-generator continuation chains across 4 domains, our distributional fingerprint features achieve macro-F1 of 0.82 for 3-class depth estimation (gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+), with leave-one-generator-out generalization at 0.80. Depth-aware data curation does not outperform random subsampling for downstream CLM quality, establishing depth fingerprinting as a diagnostic tool for provenance characterization, not a curative tool for data selection.\\\"\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n**RC1 — \\\"Is this just vocabulary impoverishment?\\\"**: Surface features alone achieve 0.76 macro-F1, but full features achieve 0.82 (p<0.001). We don't claim reference features are \\\"better\\\" — we show they capture a **different, complementary** signal (stationary distributional shape vs drifting level/diversity). The dual dynamics finding is itself a scientific contribution. Note: \\\"fingerprint\\\" in the paper refers to the full feature vector's combination, not just reference-model features.\\n\\n**RC7 — Pre-registered prediction (LD-Score)**: LD-Score (character-distribution signature) measures character-level distributional properties. We predict it is a **level feature** (sensitive to vocabulary/character frequency shifts) and should exhibit **H₂ drift** with depth. This prediction is registered before plan_011 execution as an out-of-sample test of the level/shape framework.\\n\\n**RC2 — \\\"Does this generalize beyond Pythia?\\\"**: MVP used same-family models (Pythia-2.8B generator + Pythia-410M reference). → Cross-family experiments: Qwen/OLMo generators + non-Pythia reference models (RQ1 cross-generator evaluation).\\n\\n**RC3 — \\\"Is 3-class sufficient? Why not finer-grained?\\\"**: Attractor theory bounds paraphrasing to ~3 classes. → Secondary analysis: finer-grained ordinal classification (gen-0 through gen-4) on non-paraphrastic chains to test if more depth signal exists.\\n\\n**RC4 — \\\"How realistic are single-model chains?\\\"**: Real web contamination involves diverse generators. → Cross-model chains (different generator per depth step) as primary evaluation setting (RQ3).\\n\\n**RC5 — \\\"What about human editing / post-processing?\\\"**: Real-world synthetic text is often edited. → Robustness test with simulated human edits (random word replacement as lower-bound + LLM-simulated editing).\\n\\n**RC6 — \\\"Ecological validity — continuation vs real web content\\\"**: Lab-constructed chains may not match wild distribution. → Multi-domain seeds (news, Wikipedia, scientific, creative) + multiple prompt types (continuation, elaboration, inspired rewriting).\\n\\n**RC8 — \\\"Aren't these just OOD detection features?\\\"**: Reference-model entropy statistics are functionally NLL-based OOD scores (same signal backbone as DetectGPT/GLTR/Binoculars). Our contribution is NOT the features themselves but: (a) the problem formulation (ordinal depth estimation, not binary detection), (b) the empirical discovery that these features exhibit dual dynamics (level drift vs shape stationarity) under recursive generation, and (c) the practical application to risk-stratified data curation. Paper must explicitly connect to OOD detection + perplexity-based detection literature and position the contribution as primarily empirical/conceptual rather than methodological.\\n\\n**RC9 — \\\"Only ≤2.8B generators — does this transfer to frontier scale?\\\"**: **Answered (plan-014, D011).** Qwen3-8B (7.6B params) added as 6th generator. Depth signal IS present at 8B scale — all feature-depth Spearman correlations significant (hapax ρ=-0.568, ttr ρ=-0.553, entropy_mean ρ=-0.475, all p<1e-6), confirming depth fingerprinting is a scale-invariant phenomenon. However, cross-scale transfer shows a gap: Qwen3-8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B generators 0.76-0.85 (6-gen LOGO average 0.7886, -1.1pp from 5-gen 0.80). Notably, adding 8B data improves original 5-gen classification (+0.9pp to 0.8086). **Paper framing**: depth signal universality is supported (Claim 1 holds); cross-scale classifier transfer gap reported as honest limitation with analysis (8B text is more fluent → smaller feature margins → harder to distinguish from human text). The 6-gen LOGO 0.79 still significantly outperforms all single-detector baselines.\\n\\n**RC10 — \\\"Text length confound\\\"**: Hapax ratio and TTR are mechanically length-dependent. If generation chains produce texts of systematically different lengths, surface features may track length artifacts rather than distributional drift. → Length distribution analysis + length-normalized features + length-matched comparison (plan_013). Critical confound control.\\n\\n**RC11 — \\\"Downstream utility — single run, no CIs\\\"**: Depth-aware filtering advantage must be validated with multiple seeds + bootstrap CIs + sample-count-matched comparison (to control for data size confound). Must use non-Pythia model for downstream fine-tuning (OLMo-1B) to avoid reference model circularity (Pythia-410M as both feature extractor and eval model).\\n\\n## Contribution Positioning (D006+D007)\\nThe contribution is **primarily empirical and conceptual**, not methodological:\\n1. **Problem formulation**: Ordinal depth estimation as a new task beyond binary detection (genuinely novel — no prior work)\\n2. **Empirical characterization**: Differential depth response across 6 generators / 3 families (including 7B+ scale), with robust cross-generator generalization (6-gen LOGO 0.79, family-out 0.77). Scale-invariant phenomenon with honest cross-scale transfer gap.\\n3. **Negative finding**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality — depth fingerprinting is diagnostic, not curative (D009).\\n\\n**Framing discipline (D007 — re-dream consensus):**\\n- Do NOT call the drift/stationarity split a \\\"discovery\\\" — it follows from location-shift properties of the NLL distribution (means shift under distributional drift, shapes don't). Acknowledge this explicitly.\\n- Do NOT use H1/H2 terminology (overloads time-series unit-root convention). Use \\\"drifting\\\" vs \\\"stationary\\\" or \\\"differential response.\\\"\\n- Do NOT overclaim \\\"dual dynamics\\\" as a novel theoretical framework. Use \\\"differential depth response\\\" — more calibrated.\\n- Consider renaming \\\"distributional fingerprinting\\\" → \\\"distributional depth profiling\\\" (fingerprinting implies source identification, creates confusion with LLM attribution literature).\\n- Provide at least a speculative theoretical motivation for WHY shape features remain stationary (e.g., \\\"shape is determined by sampling mechanism and architecture, invariant to input content drift\\\").\\n- Report **realistic performance range** (0.69–0.85 per-generator held-out F1, 0.79 LOGO average across 6 generators) in abstract/conclusion, not just best-case.\\n- R² on 5 aggregated depth means is statistically meaningless (3 df). Use individual-level Spearman ρ with bootstrap CIs throughout.\\n\\nRelated work must expand to 30+ references covering: perplexity-based detection (DetectGPT, GLTR, DNA-GPT, Binoculars), model collapse theory (Alemohammad et al., Dohmatob et al., Gerstgrasser et al., Guo et al.), OOD detection (Hendrycks & Gimpel), data quality scoring (DSIR, QuRating, CCNet), watermarking (Kirchenbauer et al.), vocabulary diversity (Guo et al. 2024, Padmakumar & He 2024, Holtzman et al. 2020), **stylometry/authorship attribution** (Stamatatos 2009, Koppel et al. 2009 — feature set is essentially stylometric), **iterative generation** (LLM as Broken Telephone ACL 2025, Markovian Generation Chains), **membership inference** (Shi et al. 2024).\\n\\n## Venue Fit\\n- AAAI 2027: Fit as empirical + conceptual contribution — novel task formulation (depth estimation) + surprising empirical finding (dual dynamics) + practical application (data curation). Must position as empirical science, not methodology paper.\\n- EMNLP 2026: Excellent fit — directly addresses special theme \\\"New Missions for NLP Research\\\" (data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance). NLP-native venue for text-focused work. Empirical/conceptual contributions better received here than AAAI.\\n\", \"total_chars\": 13023, \"truncated\": false}, \"error\": null, \"metadata\": {}}"}

## Target Venue
- Primary: AAAI 2027 (deadline: August 2, 2026)
- **Primary: EMNLP 2026 ARR (deadline: May 25, 2026)** — D012: 恢复为主投稿目标

## Core Insight
Non-paraphrastic LLM generation chains exhibit **differential depth response**: **central-tendency/diversity features** (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax ratio) drift monotonically with depth, while **distributional shape features** (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. This differential response is consistent with recursive generation inducing a **location shift** in the NLL distribution — the text becomes progressively more predictable (mean shifts) while the functional form of the distribution is preserved (shape is invariant). The genuine novelty is not the drift/stationarity split per se (which follows from location-shift properties), but: (a) the **task formulation** (ordinal depth estimation beyond binary detection), (b) **empirical validation** across 6 generators / 3 model families (including 7B+ scale) showing this pattern is robust, (c) the practical consequence that combining both feature types yields **complementary signal** for depth classification (macro-F1 0.79 cross-generator with 6 generators, 0.77 cross-family). Depth signal is scale-invariant as a phenomenon, though cross-scale classifier transfer shows a moderate gap (8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85).

## Core Claims (3 条，均可证伪)

**Claim 1 — Depth Discriminability**: Distributional features computed under a held-out reference model can classify text generation depth (gen-0 / gen-1 / gen-2+) with macro-F1 significantly above chance, generalizing across unseen generators (leave-one-generator-out evaluation).

**Claim 2 — Differential Depth Response & Feature Complementarity**: Depth-dependent features exhibit differential response: central-tendency/diversity features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) drift monotonically with depth (consistent with location shift in NLL distribution), while shape features (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. Full feature set (cross-gen 0.80) significantly outperforms surface-only (0.75) and reference-only (0.75) — the two feature groups are complementary. Notably, reference features generalize better across generators while surface features are stronger in-distribution — demonstrating complementarity across different evaluation axes.

**Claim 3 — Downstream Utility (Negative Finding)**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality compared to random subsampling. At equal data count, size_matched (random control, ppl=2.367) outperforms depth01 (depth-stratified, 2.387) and binary_filtered (2.389). The primary determinant is data quantity, not depth composition (all 12K samples → ppl=2.335). Depth fingerprinting is an effective **diagnostic** tool for characterizing provenance, but not a **curative** tool for data curation. This honest negative finding is reported transparently.

## Story Spine

**Problem**: Web-scraped training data increasingly contains LLM-generated text of unknown provenance depth. Current detection methods offer only binary real-vs-synthetic classification, forcing all-or-nothing filtering: discard everything flagged as synthetic (losing useful gen-1 content) or keep everything (admitting high-risk deep-generation text with compounding distributional drift).

**Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (FastDetectGPT, SynthID-Text, LD-Score) cannot distinguish gen-1 from gen-2+. Attractor cycle theory (ACL 2025) proves paraphrasing chains converge to 2-period cycles, bounding depth signal to ~3 classes — but this result depends on the semantic-preservation constraint of paraphrasing. No existing work attempts generation depth estimation. When repurposed as ordinal depth predictors, single detector scores (Avg-LogProb 0.77, LD-Score 0.72) show moderate signal but **high cross-generator variance** (CIs spanning 0.59–0.82), making them unreliable as standalone depth estimators.

**Our framing**: We characterize distributional drift in recursive non-paraphrastic LLM generation, revealing **differential depth response**: level/diversity features (including reference-model entropy_mean) drift monotonically with depth, while distributional shape features (entropy variance, tail decay) remain near-stationary. This split is about **what the feature measures** (central tendency vs shape), not where it comes from. The combination of drifting and stationary features yields a 7-feature ensemble (LOGO F1=0.80 [0.786, 0.799]) that **significantly and consistently** outperforms all single-detector baselines (p<0.001 vs Avg-LogProb 0.77, LD-Score 0.72, FastDetectGPT 0.63, Binoculars 0.58). Crucially, single detectors exhibit high cross-generator variance (CIs spanning 0.59–0.82), while our ensemble maintains tight consistency — the practical advantage is **reliability across unknown generators**, not just average performance.

**Headline result template**: "On multi-generator continuation chains across 4 domains, our distributional fingerprint features achieve macro-F1 of 0.82 for 3-class depth estimation (gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+), with leave-one-generator-out generalization at 0.80. **RC1 — "Is this just vocabulary impoverishment?"**: Surface features alone achieve 0.76 macro-F1, but full features achieve 0.82 (p<0.001). We don't claim reference features are "better" — we show they capture a **different, complementary** signal (stationary distributional shape vs drifting level/diversity). The dual dynamics finding is itself a scientific contribution. Note: "fingerprint" in the paper refers to the full feature vector's combination, not just reference-model features.

This prediction is registered before plan_011 execution as an out-of-sample test of the level/shape framework.

**RC4 — "How realistic are single-model chains?"**: Real web contamination involves diverse generators. → Cross-model chains (different generator per depth step) as primary evaluation setting (RQ3).

**RC5 — "What about human editing / post-processing?"**: Real-world synthetic text is often edited. → Robustness test with simulated human edits (random word replacement as lower-bound + LLM-simulated editing).

**RC6 — "Ecological validity — continuation vs real web content"**: Lab-constructed chains may not match wild distribution. → Multi-domain seeds (news, Wikipedia, scientific, creative) + multiple prompt types (continuation, elaboration, inspired rewriting).

Paper must explicitly connect to OOD detection + perplexity-based detection literature and position the contribution as primarily empirical/conceptual rather than methodological.

**RC9 — "Only ≤2.8B generators — does this transfer to frontier scale?"**: **Answered (plan-014, D011).** Qwen3-8B (7.6B params) added as 6th generator. The 6-gen LOGO 0.79 still significantly outperforms all single-detector baselines.

**RC10 — "Text length confound"**: Hapax ratio and TTR are mechanically length-dependent. If generation chains produce texts of systematically different lengths, surface features may track length artifacts rather than distributional drift. → Length distribution analysis + length-normalized features + length-matched comparison (plan_013). Critical confound control.

**RC11 — "Downstream utility — single run, no CIs"**: Depth-aware filtering advantage must be validated with multiple seeds + bootstrap CIs + sample-count-matched comparison (to control for data size confound). Must use non-Pythia model for downstream fine-tuning (OLMo-1B) to avoid reference model circularity (Pythia-410M as both feature extractor and eval model).

1. **Problem formulation**: Ordinal depth estimation as a new task beyond binary detection (genuinely novel — no prior work)

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

We evaluate depth fingerprinting along four axes: cross-generator classification (\S\ref{sec:results-classification}), differential depth response of individual features (\S\ref{sec:results-differential}), comparison with existing detection baselines (\S\ref{sec:results-baselines}), and downstream utility for data curation (\S\ref{sec:results-downstream}).

\subsection{Depth Classification Performance}
\label{sec:results-classification}

Table~\ref{tab:logo-results} reports leave-one-generator-out (LOGO) macro-F1 for 3-class depth estimation (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) across six generators spanning three model families and parameter counts from 0.6B to 8.2B.

The 7-feature ensemble achieves LOGO F1\,=\,0.790 (95\% bootstrap CI [0.786, 0.799]), significantly outperforming all single-detector baselines ($p<0.001$; \S\ref{sec:results-baselines}).
Per-generator held-out F1 ranges from 0.685 (Qwen3-8B) to 0.855 (Pythia-1B).

\textbf{Variant} & \textbf{$n$} & \textbf{Test PPL} \\
\midrule
